result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.disjoint_union_all()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Place any number of graphs side by side with `disjoint_union()`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L30109-L30150){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.disjoint_union_all(graphs) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Disjoint union of many graphs](/assets/graphs/disjoint-union-all.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three separate pieces, each numbered from 1: a triangle (accent), a path of 4 nodes (teal), and a star of 5 nodes (violet). disjoint_union_all never merges ids: the triangle keeps ids 1 to 3, the path is renumbered 4 to 7 and the star 8 to 12, giving 12 nodes, 10 edges, and 3 connected components." width="100%"} Applies `disjoint_union()` from left to right: each graph's nodes are renumbered above the previous ones, so nothing is merged and the result has one copy of every graph. Clashing labels get numeric suffixes. Use it to run one analysis over many separate networks at once, or to build test graphs with several components. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [graphs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A non-empty list of graphs with the same directedness. None is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph whose node and edge counts are the sums over all graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the list is empty or the graphs differ in directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Equivalent to chaining `disjoint_union()`. Mirrors NetworkX's `disjoint_union_all`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#174e0a22 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec pieces = [ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(3), ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4), ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5)] combined = ec.Graph.disjoint_union_all(pieces) combined.count_nodes(), combined.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (12, 3) ``` ::: :::
